_comment: T1 item 6 `not_applicable` STATEMENT for the DIGITAL partition (issue
#562): one entry per row of digital-partition-spec.json -- exactly those
rows, none more, none fewer (`klt signoff` refuses otherwise). `class`
names the kind of row; `reason` says why that kind is not statistical.
WHAT THIS CLAIMS: that no row the digital partition owns is a
distribution-valued requirement, so Monte Carlo evidence has nothing to
attach to. It is a claim about the row CLASS, not about whether the rows
are met: timing and the rung-2 gate-level replay are graded by item 5,
WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER: the analog partition (6.analog cites `klt yield`
evidence and may never use this form), and any whole-ADC row. If a
statistical digital row is ever ratified, this statement stops being
true and 6.digital must move to `klt yield` evidence instead.

rows.reason: The 10-bit width is a count fixed by construction: ten comparator trials (DR-0009, plain binary, no redundancy) loaded into a ten-bit output register. It takes the same value on every corner and every die, so there is no spread to bound.

The requirement on sar_ctrl is that it closes timing at the 62.5 ns period (16 MHz, DR-0003). Static timing analysis bounds that at the PDK's characterised corners (`klt sta`, five gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu7t5v0 corners; design/sar-logic/flow/sar_ctrl/records/20260915-093934-7ab8971.mcu7t5v0.sta_postroute.md). The corner is the whole condition; no statistical bound is claimed or checked.

A synchronous sequencer (DR-0008) takes exactly 4 sample + 10 bit-trial + 2 reset/output clocks per conversion, so latency is M = 16 clock periods at every corner and on every die. A cycle count is exact; it is checked by simulating the sequence, not by sampling a distribution.

The row says what interface exists: a parallel output register, with SPI deferred (DR-0005). Whether it exists and carries the ten decisions is pass/fail structural and functional behaviour, not a measured quantity with a spread.
